title: Emulator — Network
description: Inter-tier network behaviour per node-to-node link: latency (configured one-way vs measured one-way) and bandwidth (configured cap vs measured throughput). The configured values are declarative — the template declares them and the controller does not implement them, so the measured values reflect the real cluster path. Latency is shown one-way (the measured TCP round-trip halved) to line up with the configured one-way panel; throughput is the measured iperf3 egress summed across the source role's pods.

list.name: base_ms
list.label: Base one-way RTT to subtract (ms)
list.description: Unshaped base network latency between nodes, optionally subtracted from the measured value. ~half the node-to-node round-trip base (≈3ms here). Set 0 to see the raw measurement.

panels.title: Configured latency between nodes
panels.description: One-way latency configured in the template's network_links for each site pair (e.g. edge_01 -> fog_01 = 10ms means 10ms A→B and 10ms B→A). Updates immediately on PATCH.

panels.title: Measured one-way latency between nodes — min / avg / max (selected period)
panels.description: One row per node-to-node link (source tier → destination tier), averaged across the source pods, over the selected time range — one-way (the measured TCP round-trip halved). Compare it against the configured panel above to see how the real cluster path compares to what the template declares; they match only if a separate system provisions the link. The unshaped base RTT can be subtracted via the `base_ms` control at the top (set it to 0 to see the raw measurement).

panels.title: One-way latency between nodes (time series)
panels.description: Measured one-way latency for each node-to-node link (source tier → destination tier), averaged across the source pods, over the selected time range — set the range with the dashboard time picker (top-right) to see the last X minutes. TCP round-trip halved, probed every 15s; this is the real cluster network path. The unshaped base RTT can be subtracted via the `base_ms` control at the top (set it to 0 for the raw measurement).

panels.title: Configured bandwidth between nodes
panels.description: Bandwidth cap declared in the template's network_links for each site pair (e.g. edge_01 ↔ fog_01 = 1000mbps). Declarative — it describes the cap for another system to enforce; the controller does not enforce it. Updates immediately on PATCH. Compare the measured throughput panels below against it.

panels.title: Throughput between nodes (time series)
panels.description: Measured egress throughput for each node-to-node link (source tier → destination tier), summed across the source role's pods, from worker_peer_egress_mbps (parsed from the iperf3 client's per-second interval reports). This is the actual traffic crossing the link; compare it against the declared bandwidth cap above. Values are converted to bits/sec so Grafana auto-scales to Mb/s.

panels.title: Measured throughput between nodes — min / avg / max (selected period)
panels.description: One row per node-to-node link (source tier → destination tier), summed across the source role's pods, over the selected time range. Avg is the steady-state throughput on the link; Max approaches the configured `bandwidth` cap when the link saturates. Values are bits/sec (auto-scaled to Mb/s).
